historical_references.reference: Maqsyud al-Idrisi was a 12th-century Muslim geographer, cartographer and traveler from Sicily. He is best known for his Book of Rogues (Ahsan al-Taqasim fi Marifat al-Aqalim), which describes the geography of the known Islamic world along with its regions and people. His works significantly influenced European cartography for centuries.
historical_references.context: Islamic Sicily, Andalusia, North Africa and Spain

historical_references.reference: The name 'Maqsyud' is also attributed to a famous Sufi saint of the Chishti order in India, Sheikh Muinuddin Chishti.
